record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports direction measurements and steering interventions, including an explicit result that the single-direction hypothesis does not fit Gemma-3-1b-it. Its findings refine the claim by model and intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports probe, direction-similarity, activation-steering, and activation-guided optimization results. The reported transferability, perplexity, and topic-relevance results do not measure the listed claim versions. The GCG results are not counted as evidence for V3: the README describes optimization toward compliance activations, not suppression of the direction.
record.test_reason: The README reports runtime steering along a refusal/compliance direction, with behavioural outcomes on Gemma-3-1b-it and two Turkish Kumru models. It also argues explicitly that the single-direction hypothesis fails for Gemma. Its direction contrasts each harmful prompt with the same prompt plus a forced 'Sure, here is' prefix, not harmful minus harmless. Its intervention is activation addition, not directional ablation. It is a GitHub README with no uncertainty estimates and very small prompt sets (10–15).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the README claims Gemma-3-1b-it showed 'absolute resilience (100% defense rate)' to steering and GCG. It also says the 0.3711 cosine 'invalidates' the single-direction hypothesis for Gemma, an inference its evidence does not establish.
record.recipe_differences: Tool repo, not a stated replication. It uses logistic-regression probe directions, multi-layer activation references, runtime steering, and activation-guided GCG. It reports no projection-out ablation or weight edit, and uses forced compliance continuations to collect compliance activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model, intervention depth, and steering strength. Gemma single-layer L8 steering is reported ineffective; Turkish Kumru results vary by model and alpha, with alpha=4 and alpha=5 described as degenerate repetition rather than meaningful success.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma, GCG suffixes pushed forced-target activations into the compliance region (10/10), yet free generation still refused (0/10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Moving activations into a compliance region at one position need not change refusal behaviour in free generation.

record.problems: The README reports small prompt counts for key behavioral tests (10 prompts for Gemma GCG and 15 for Turkish steering), and describes Turkish jailbreak candidates as heuristic. No general-capability retention evaluation or uncertainty estimates are reported. The Gemma steering test is single-layer, not the all-layer intervention in V1. The repository outputs are described as git-ignored, and the README/file list alone was available here.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible result rows omitted. The README's Qwen GCG success and transferability results do not specifically test suppression of the direction (V3); perplexity and topic-relevance results do not measure any listed version.

Any analysis of dimensionality (affine, cone, multiple directions). The cosine evidence offered cannot address it.

Separating the harm judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages or models. Directions are computed separately per model, and the kumru-base profile has no reported results.
Effect of training method or stage.

record.verdict_notes: Read the README only. The direction contrasts refusal with forced-compliance activations on harmful prompts, so it is not Arditi et al.'s harmful-minus-harmless direction. Probe/mean-difference cosines do not measure dimensionality, so no V4 verdict is given despite the README's claim. The Gemma steering failure is single-layer and should not be read as an ablation result. Kumru behaviour labels are heuristic, and the alpha was chosen after the sweep.

versions.untested_parts: No all-layer-and-position ablation; no steering toward refusal on harmless requests; no broad evaluation of retained general capability. Steering and direction results are limited to the stated models and settings.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration results.
No test that attacks suppress the direction, or that training against its ablation improves robustness.
No explicit affine or cone analysis; the README reports probe/difference-of-means similarity and interprets Gemma results as multi-dimensional.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language or cross-model transfer of a direction; the listed models have separate profiles and evaluations.
No controlled comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
